pr_title: Also migrate dsmr entries for devices with correct serial
pr_body:
When the dsmr code could not find the serial_nr for the gas meter, it creates the gas meter device with the entry_id as identifier.

But when there is a correct serial_nr, it will use that as identifier for the dsmr gas device.

Now the migration code did not take this into account, so migration to the new name failed since it didn't look for the device with correct serial_nr.

This commit fixes this and adds a test for this.

issue_context.body:
### The problem

After updating to 2024.8 beta (it stopped in the latest nightly before the beta) the gas meter is not working correctly anymore. This might to be related to [Upgrade dsmr-parser to 1.4.2 #121929](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/121929)?

Normally the integration adds two sensors. Current usage and total usage.
The current usage one is disabled and reports the entity is not available anymore from the integration.
The total usage sensor is still working.

core-2024.8.0b1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

pre core-2024.8.0b0

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

DSMR Smart Meter

https://rc.home-assistant.io/integrations/dsmr

This ends up switching the prefix. I'm not sure this make sense. The hourly_gas_meter_reading is still in use for {"4", "5", "5L"} according to our setup.

The `hourly_gas_meter_reading` will not be used anymore if there are mbus devices.
And as the code is only executed when there are mbus devices. This should work fine :)

What i also meant is, the unique id could be prefixed with the gas serial or the entry unique id. Both these cases now get transformed to the gas serial unique id.

But if you are sure that is okey...
We could look for a device with entry.data[CONF_SERIAL_ID_GAS]?

In fact we should stop using CONF_SERIAL_ID_GAS for devices with mbus devices.
Cause `CONF_SERIAL_ID_GAS` is a single entity ... while with mbus we have 4 devices that can be linked to the main device, so you can have 4 gas meters in theory.
Better check for the mbus_device_id.
How you mean? There should be only 1 main SERIAL for the device and then a serial per mbus device.

I am not sure what il saying. I think i would have been more happy with doing a full unique_id check and just iterate over all entities in the config entry instead of per device.

Unique_id, should be just that,  unique for the integration. The associated device have nothing to do with it really.

The replacements should be static once we know the serial.

{serial_gas}_hourly.. -> serial_gas.
{serial_main}_hourly -> ? (Do we even know these exist?)

But there is no advantage afaik to loop over all entities. Cause with this patch we loop over all the devices that can match already.
If there would be more dsmr devices, this won't match anyway when doing a full unique_id check, as the serial in it should be the same as the device serial, and thus different anyway. So useless to lookup.

Only since https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/91182603d5756c38714f4c21d5cd6e04f1522d2b the correct serial is used for gas meters in 5B. That's why the migration code was working fine for 5B in the past, as entry_id was used and not the correct serial.
But for 5 (and now also 5B), the real gas serial is used, so we need to use that to lookup the device.

Also note that with supporting multiple mbus devices, its possible that you now have 1 gas meter, but with the multiple mbus support, it will see both gas meters.
So we need to make sure here to migrate the existing sensor to the correct device.

But migrating the sensor to the correct/new device is better/cleaner, as before https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/91182603d5756c38714f4c21d5cd6e04f1522d2b for example the device did not have the correct serial like it should.
The current migration code takes care of that also.

If there is no mbus data, then the migration code will not be run. So that shouldn't cause an issue?

I still don't like doing a `RANDOM_PREFIX_THAT_CAN_BE_ANYTHINGhourly_gas_meter_reading` -> `mbus_device_id`. It's very error prone.
